claims.subject_operation: Concurrent transaction writers appending to one SQLite database WAL
claims.version_configuration: WAL since SQLite 3.7.0; target 3.51.3, normal shared-memory-capable VFS, multiple processes, one local database
claims.default_type_unit_domain: One writer per database/WAL; concurrency of readers with a writer is a different operation
claims.exceptions_checked: No supplied condition permits concurrent writers to the same WAL. Separate databases, proxy deployment and unsupported experimental branches do not change this case. Ordinary writer contention can wait or return BUSY according to busy handling.
claims.corrected_bounded_meaning: Writers serialize; readers may coexist with the current writer.

claims.subject_operation: Long-lived read snapshot versus checkpoint backfill, reset and ongoing WAL growth
claims.version_configuration: Target 3.51.3, ordinary WAL; nominal automatic checkpoint threshold 1000 pages absent overrides
claims.default_type_unit_domain: 1000 is pages, not bytes. WAL growth requires continued writes; full backfill and WAL reset are distinct. Both compile-time and run-time checkpoint settings can change defaults.
claims.exceptions_checked: Reader snapshot end mark determines backfill boundary; current-snapshot readers need not make backfill incomplete. Disabled checkpoints and large write transactions are independent growth causes. RESTART/TRUNCATE can wait for readers and return BUSY.
claims.corrected_bounded_meaning: An old read snapshot can prevent completion/reset while later committed frames accumulate. The body preserves continued writes; acceptance check 1 drops that necessary setup.

claims.default_type_unit_domain: Conditions are alternatives: readable -wal AND -shm; directory permitting their creation; or an immutable connection. immutable is a boolean URI parameter, not a locking flag for a mutable live DB.
claims.exceptions_checked: URI processing must be enabled; this prerequisite is preserved in candidate A1 source evidence and source-map, though abbreviated in verification.md. Immutable files must remain unmodifiable; otherwise incorrect results/CORRUPT are possible. The WAL is persistent state when present. claims.subject_operation: Successful PASSIVE sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 invocation versus zero-byte WAL guarantee
claims.version_configuration: Target 3.51.3, database actually in WAL mode, selected checkpoint mode
claims.default_type_unit_domain: pnLog/pnCkpt are integer frame counts, not byte lengths. PASSIVE does not invoke the busy handler; TRUNCATE adds zero-byte truncation before successful return.
claims.exceptions_checked: Checkpoint-lock contention returns BUSY without a handler; FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE may fall back to PASSIVE-like progress with BUSY if the handler gives up. NULL/empty database selector leaves aggregate frame outputs undefined. A non-WAL DB is a successful no-op with -1 outputs. journal_size_limit can affect retained file size but does not turn every PASSIVE success into a truncation guarantee. A concurrent later write can grow a WAL after the operation returns.
claims.corrected_bounded_meaning: PASSIVE is best effort and does not guarantee a zero-byte file. In this WAL checkpoint interface, successful TRUNCATE supplies that operation-specific guarantee.

material_findings.candidate_text: Hold a long read, run PASSIVE — expect incomplete checkpoint, no reset

independent_primary_locators.section: 2.2 Concurrency: snapshot end mark and checkpoint boundary
PASSIVE completion can occur; FULL permits current-snapshot readers; RESTART adds reader clearance

material_findings.source_statement: Readers keep a fixed snapshot end mark; checkpoint backfill stops at frames beyond that mark. PASSIVE may leave a checkpoint unfinished, but it can backfill all available frames. FULL can copy all frames while readers see the latest snapshot; RESTART adds a distinct wait so the WAL may restart.
material_findings.reviewer_inference: A reader seeing the newest commit, with no later commits, can coexist with complete backfill. An empty/fully backfilled WAL is also a permitted state. Merely holding a reader therefore does not imply pnCkpt < pnLog. Lack of reset is distinct from incomplete backfill.
material_findings.consequence: The first required acceptance check can reject a conforming target deployment or fail to exercise checkpoint starvation. Its deterministic incomplete-checkpoint oracle does not follow from its specified setup. This is a missing causal precondition, not a demand for execution or a detailed test harness.
material_findings.bounded_diagnostic: Pin an actual reader snapshot, commit frames beyond its end mark from another connection, verify an incomplete PASSIVE backfill using the selected WAL database and frame outputs, then release the reader and check a successful TRUNCATE with other transactions quiescent.
material_findings.countervailing_candidate_support: The claim-2 body at lines 23-24 correctly says continued writes. This finding preserves that supported body and concerns the acceptance criterion that omits the necessary write-after-snapshot setup.
material_findings.actual_execution: No candidate local probe was executed; candidate source-map explicitly marks this as prospective. Reviewer also did not execute a target-version service probe.
